courses.title: Applied Inquiry and Research Design
courses.description: Introduction to Kinesiology and Health Promotion research through the critical examination of literature and application of key principles, culminating in the design and development of a research proposal. Topics include: theoretical and technical facets of planning and performing research, crafting research questions, research ethics and methodologies.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Data Literacy, Analysis, and Synthesis
courses.description: Exploration of key data and analytical model concepts in Kinesiology and Health Promotion research, culminating in the design, development and implementation of a full research proposal. Topics include: applied research methods, statistical and qualitative analytical methods, analytical software, interpretation of results, data synthesis, and pilot evaluation.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Critical Analysis of Research
courses.description: Critical evaluation of health and human movement literature to promote and broaden student understanding of research within our field. Emphasis is placed on developing an interdisciplinary understanding through an active-learning pedagogy approach.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of the instructor.

courses.title: Research Colloquium
courses.description: Strategies used to disseminate health and human movement research to academic and non-academic audiences. Content includes research presentations and skill-based workshops. Emphasis is placed on developing an interdisciplinary understanding of the field through an active-learning pedagogy approach.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Practicing Professional Competencies
courses.description: Provides students with the knowledge and skills needed to advance their career goals. Emphasis will be placed on developing the professional competencies required to be model, dynamic, and adaptable leaders in the Kinesiology and Health Promotion field.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Teaching Performance Assessment for Secondary Teachers
courses.description: Single subject candidates connect theory to practice as they apply and reflect on their teaching practice and professional behaviors based on classroom equity, professional responsibilities, and Teacher Performance Expectations. Candidates complete the Teaching Performance Assessment and develop a plan for continuing their growth on the California Standards for the Teaching Profession. Corequisite(s): EDU 5260 or EDU 5420 .
courses.prerequisites: Admitted to Single Subject Credential, EDU 5205 or TED 434, EDU 5210 or TED 442, EDU 5215 or TED 446, and EDU 5220 .

courses.title: Practicing Pedagogical Competencies
courses.description: Provides students an opportunity to participate in a supportive community of practice. Emphasis will be placed on developing the pedagogical competencies required to be model, inclusive, and adaptable educators in health and human movement. Corequisite(s): Employment as a KHP Graduate Teaching Associate.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 3 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Individual study/investigation and research in a specialized area proposed by the student with the approval, and under the supervision, of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Project
courses.description: The Kinesiology and Health Promotion project is the translation of empirical evidence to create and defend an applied artifact relevant to the chosen field of practice. The finished product evidences originality, critical and independent thinking, appropriate organization and format, and thorough documentation.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 5900 and KIN 5910 with an average grade of B or better, KIN 5920 , and KIN 5930 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.description: The Kinesiology and Health Promotion thesis is the written product and oral defense of a systematic study of a significant problem. The finished product evidences originality, critical and independent thinking, appropriate organization and format, and thorough documentation.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 5900 and KIN 5910 with a B grade or better, KIN 5920 , and KIN 5930 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 or 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 1 or 3 units per semester; dependent on curriculum year.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Comprehensive Exams
courses.description: The Kinesiology and Health Promotion Comprehensive Exams are an assessment of the student’s ability to integrate the knowledge of the area, show critical and independent thinking, and demonstrate a mastery of the subject matter. The assessments consist of three elements: 1) critical analysis presentation; 2) written exams; and 3) oral defense.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Graduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
